full_judgment:
7. Mr. Faruque Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant appellants has submitted that in the absence of a positive finding of possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land within 12 years prior to the institution of the suit, the learned Subordinate Judge committed an error of law in affixing the decree of the trial court. He has submitted that in terms of Article 142 of the Limitation Act, the plaintiffs are to prove their possession within 12 years of the institution of the suit by positive evidence and that presumption of possession that possession follows title cannot be availed of in lieu of actual physical possession i.e. the person having title would not be deemed to be in possession within 12 years of the institution of the suit under Article 142 of the Limitation Act. In my view if the evidence of possession of behalf of the plaintiffs and on behalf of the defendants as to the former's possession within 12 years before suit is evenly balanced the presumption that possession goes with title shall prevail where the evidence adduced by both the parties, although unsatisfactory is not together valueless, the court is entitled to take into consideration the presumption arises from title. In this view the learned Subordinate Judge correctly held that the plaintiffs should be deemed to be in possession of the suit land within 12 years before the institution of the suit. 

 8. I, therefore, find no substance in the contention on behalf of the defendant appellants, that is the absence of a positive finding of possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land within 12 years prior to the institution of the suit, the learned Subordinate Judge committed an error of law in affirming the decree of the trial court. The presumptive possession of the plaintiffs in the land on proof of their title in the facts of the case would be sufficient to discharge the onus of proving possession because presumption is an inference as to existence of a fact from the existence of some other founded fact.
